In [[Mathematics]], the '''Mashreghi–Ransford inequality''' is a bound on the growth rate of certain [[sequences]].  It is named after [[Javad Mashreghi|J.&nbsp;Mashreghi]] and [[Thomas Ransford|T.&nbsp;Ransford]].

Let <math>(a_n)_{n \geq 0}</math> be a sequence of [[complex number]]s, and let

: <math> b_n = \sum_{k=0}^n {n\choose k} a_k, \qquad (n \geq 0),</math>

and

: <math> c_n = \sum_{k=0}^n (-1)^{k} {n\choose k} a_k, \qquad (n \geq 0).</math>

Here the [[binomial coefficients]] are defined by

: <math> {n\choose k} = \frac{n!}{k! (n-k)!}.</math>

Assume that, for some <math>\beta>1</math>, we have <math>b_n = O(\beta^n)</math> and <math>c_n = O(\beta^n)</math> as <math>n \to \infty</math>. Then Mashreghi-Ransford showed that

: <math>a_n = O(\alpha^n)</math>, as <math>n \to \infty</math>,

where <math>\alpha=\sqrt{\beta^2-1}.</math> Moreover, there is a [[universal constant]] <math>\kappa</math> such that

:<math> \left( \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{|a_n|}{\alpha^n} \right) \leq \kappa \, \left( \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{|b_n|}{\beta^n} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}  \left( \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{|c_n|}{\beta^n} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}.</math>

The precise value of <math>\kappa</math> is still unknown. However, it is known that

: <math> \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\leq \kappa \leq 2.</math>
